simple.meaning: תֻּמָּה (tummâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “innocence.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: תֻּמָּה (H8538) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Job 2:3, with occurrences in Job, Proverbs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תֻּמָּה (H8538) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in תֻּמָּה (H8538) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: תֻּמָּה (tummâh) / H8538 is traced through Job 2:3, Job 2:9, Job 27:5, Job 31:6 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Yahweh said to Satan, “Have you considered my servant Job? For there is no one like him in the earth, a blameless and an upright man, one who fears God, and turns away from evil. He still maintains his integrity, although you incited me against him, to ruin him without cause.”

timeline.evidenceText: Yahweh said to Satan, “Have you considered my servant Job? For there is no one like him in the earth, a blameless and an upright man, one who fears God, and turns away from evil. He still maintains his integrity, although you incited me against him, to ruin him without cause.”
Then his wife said to him, “Do you still maintain your integrity? Renounce God, and die.”
Far be it from me that I should justify you.
